body:
## Summary
The candidate send gate (consent, erasure, agent population, opt-out for outreach) runs only inside `sendComm`, i.e. AFTER every invite door has already minted a live capability link. Lift the verdict into one pure-plus-adapter module in this context and have every link-minting door ask it BEFORE the mint.

## Description
`commsSendSuppression` (app/_lib/comms.ts:290) is correctly the single predicate the channel enforces, but the doors that mint candidate links ask a narrower question first: the bulk planner and the stage hooks check addressability only (bulk-invite.ts:43-46, stage-hooks.ts:259, stage-hooks-homework.ts:143) and the single invite route checks only `status` (schedule/invite/route.ts:65). A candidate whose consent has lapsed but who has not yet been swept by `anonymizeExpiredConsents` still has a contact, so each door mints a working `/schedule/<token>` (or burns an AI-interview grounding build and voice minutes, or publishes a case apply token), the dispatch then throws `CommsSuppressedError`, the route swallows it and reports `{ok:true, token}` - and the bulk response counts it in `sent`. The link exists, the recruiter can copy it from the drawer's copy panel, and nothing in the result says why the letter did not go.

New `app/_lib/comms-contactability.ts`: a pure `contactVerdict(facts, kind)` ordering reasons by irreversibility (agent population -> consent/anonymized -> opt-out for kind 'outreach' only -> unaddressable), plus a server adapter `entryContactability(entry, kind)` that gathers the facts through the existing `candidateOutreachSuppression`/`outreachHaltFor` reads (no new query). The recipient cascade moves into `comms-recipient.ts` (pure, import-free as that file requires) and bulk-invite.ts drops its duplicate. Consumers: bulk planner + route (per-entry `COMMS_SUPPRESSED`, no mint), single invite route (409 `COMMS_SUPPRESSED` before `createScheduleInvite`), stage-hooks (new reason `suppressed`, skipped WITHOUT parking), homework hook (same). comms-dispatch.ts is deliberately NOT touched (r08 pipeline-candidate-drawer rewrites it); its own copy of the cascade at :72 becomes a one-line delegation as a named follow-up after r08 lands.

Surfaces that offer the refused action or display the refusal: the bulk bar (usePipelineBulk.ts:284, folds per-entry codes through errors.<CODE> - :163, :280), the drawer's link minter (PipelineTokenLink.tsx:20-24, resolves the code via useErrorMessage), the Schedule tab (useScheduleTab.ts:276, returns the body to the card's refusal line), and the guided sim (useSimulationWalk.ts:486, sim titles bypass the channel but not this gate - the sim seeds consent, verify in the test). All four already render a coded refusal and COMMS_SUPPRESSED is already in all four catalogs, so no UI file is in the write set; the builder must confirm each by reading, not assume.

Read->write strategy: verdict-then-mint is a read followed by a write with no lock; the dispatch-time gate in comms.ts stays as the RE-CHECK, so a consent that lapses between verdict and send is still refused at the channel. No transaction is added.

## Flow
1. Write comms-contactability.test.ts cases 1-3 (pure) and the bulk/single/stage-hook cases red.
2. Add the cascade export to comms-recipient.ts; point bulk-invite.ts at it.
3. Add contactVerdict + entryContactability.
4. Wire bulk route, single route, stage-hooks.ts, stage-hooks-homework.ts.
5. Docs: comms README (the gate now runs pre-mint on invite doors) and scheduling README (bulk result vocabulary).

## Expected impact
No live scheduling / interview / case link is ever minted for a person the send gate would refuse; the bulk count stops claiming invites that were legally blocked; AI-interview spend is not burned on a suppressed arrival; and the send policy has one more-complete chokepoint instead of three narrower pre-checks.

## Evaluation
Claim: every candidate-link mint door refuses a suppressed candidate before minting, with the same reason the channel would give.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass.
After: 8 of 8.
Method: node:test - pure verdict cases, route tests over a temp KP_DB_PATH (bulk + single), stage-hook tests; plus tsc, lint, i18n:check, test:unit.
Result: pending build.
Gate: policy-tighten.

title: Wrong-language letters get a candidate fix: pick our language on the stop page
acceptance: POST /api/stop/<valid token>/language {locale:'en'} -> 200 {locale:'en'}; the token's entry has locale='en' and locale_chosen_at set; a sibling entry with the same candidate_id in the SAME workspace is also 'en'; an entry with that candidate_id in ANOTHER workspace is untouched

app/stop/[token]/StopClient.tsx:7,127-129 already offers a LanguageSwitcher - but it changes only the PAGE's language; the letters stay in the stored locale
app/api/stop/[token]/route.ts:49-59 stopView is an explicit allowlist projection; :91-110 POST resolves the entry by opt-out token and takes the tenant off the row, never a session
app/_lib/auth/public-routes.ts:90 admits the '/api/stop/' subtree (strict descendants), so /api/stop/[token]/language is already public - no public-routes change

rollback: Three commits (schema column + store + comms-locale preference and the two scoped callers; the /language route + projection + contract pin + api-reference; the page control + catalogs) revert in reverse order. The column is additive (ALTER ADD COLUMN locale_chosen_at TEXT, nullable), so reverting the code leaves a harmless unused column; entries whose locale a candidate chose keep that locale, which is the correct residue.
runner_up: Recruiter outreach control on the board: expose sends/replied/opted-out per entry and wire the dead haltOutreach/resumeOutreach (outreach-state-store.ts:202-206 'NOT YET REACHABLE FROM THE UI') - traded away because every surface that would display it (candidate drawer, rediscovery feed) is in an r08 write set.
body:
## Summary
A candidate reading our letter in the wrong language has no way to fix it: the explicit choice the locale authority ranks first can only be captured at apply time, and the CV inference prefers Czech whenever Czech appears at all. Turn the unsubscribe page - the one candidate door every letter already links - into the place a candidate says 'write to me in English', stored as an explicit, person-level choice that later inference respects.

## Description
The registry technique (candidate-locale-resolution-authority, step 3) says the unrecorded case should be 'corrected the moment the candidate tells you anything' and (step 4) that the destination page 'still offers its own language control ... exercising the same recorded choice'. kp's stop page has the control (StopClient.tsx:128) but it is cosmetic: it flips the page and nothing else.

Build: an additive `locale_chosen_at` column on pipeline_entries marks a stored locale as the candidate's own choice. `setCandidateChosenLocale(entryId, locale, workspaceId)` is ONE UPDATE over the token's entry and every entry sharing its non-empty candidate_id inside the SAME workspace (the tenant comes off the token's row, like the stop write) - no read-compute-write, last choice wins by design, so no lock is needed. `inferProfileLocale(candidateId, workspaceId)` asks for a chosen locale first and only then infers from CV languages, and the two routes that call it unscoped (outreach :122, pipeline :139) pass the `ws` they already hold, so the choice and the inference both work outside the default team. New public POST /api/stop/[token]/language (admitted by public-routes.ts:90's subtree; own limiter pinned in the contract test; one new refusal code STOP_LANGUAGE_INVALID -> REFUSAL_ERRORS + errors.* in all four catalogs). GET's allowlist gains `letterLocale` + `localeChosen`. The page offers, above the stop panel, 'Our letters to you are in <language>' with a one-click 'write to me in <the language you are reading this page in>' when those differ (pure `stopLanguageOffer`), plus a select for the other two. It never touches the opt-out: choosing a language is not stopping, and the scope copy stays as is.

No new automation event kind (the event vocabulary is pinned by set equality across three registries, stage-hooks.ts:332-334); the column timestamp is the record. No recruiter surface displays the chosen flag in this card; every letter, the offer-letter preview (comms-letter-preview.ts:87) and the schedule/interview link pins already resolve through resolveCommsLocale, so they follow the choice with no change.

## Flow
1. Red tests: route cases, projection allowlist, inferProfileLocale preference, stopLanguageOffer.
2. core.ts ALTER + pipeline.ts setter/reader; comms-locale.ts preference; scope the two callers.
3. /language route + GET projection + contract pin + `npm run api:docs`.
4. StopClient control + 4-locale copy (under the shared-surface lock).
5. comms README: the explicit-choice capture points now include the stop page.

## Expected impact
A candidate misaddressed by inference (the Czech tiebreak, a workspace default) fixes every future letter, link and new-role entry in one click, from a link they already have; recruiters stop sending bank letters a candidate cannot read; and two live tenant misses in locale inference close on the way.

## Evaluation
Claim: a candidate can set the language of all our future letters from the stop page, without opting out, and later inference respects it.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass.
After: 7 of 7.
Method: node:test route tests over a temp KP_DB_PATH, pure stopLanguageOffer tests, inferProfileLocale test; plus tsc, lint, i18n:check, api:check, test:unit.
Result: pending build.
Gate: contract.
